name: Kit Clark Furniture
old_description: It is the honor of my career to bring beauty and balance into my client's homes. The true reward in doing what I do is seeing the impact my furniture has on the people who interact with it on a daily basis.
about:
Kit Clark Furniture operates from a studio in North Yarmouth, Maine, a rural community northwest of Portland. The business traces its roots to the early 2000s when founder Kit Clark opened a shop in Bozeman, Montana, after studying furniture design at the Penland School of Crafts in North Carolina. Clark relocated the operation to North Ferrisburgh, Vermont, in 2000, then moved again in the spring of 2016 to the current Maine location. A lifelong woodworker, Clark earned an associate degree in forestry from the University of New Hampshire and a bachelor’s in mine land reclamation from Montana State University, later apprenticing under his uncle, master carpenter Robert Clark, and studying Sam Maloof–style rocking chairs with chairwright Hal Taylor in 2007.

The studio produces bespoke, handcrafted furniture ranging from sculpted rocking chairs and dining sets to tables, beds, bedroom suites, bookcases, and custom accessories. Each piece is built to order using traditional joinery and a selection of domestic and exotic woods chosen by the client. Clark works alone or with minimal assistance, fabricating every component in-house and finishing each item to a museum-quality standard. Output is measured in individual commissions rather than volume runs, with no published capacity figures.

The clientele consists primarily of residential customers across the continental United States and Canada, including homeowners and interior designers seeking one-of-a-kind heirloom pieces. Testimonials reference clients in North Carolina, Singapore, and Massachusetts, and the company offers in-home design consultations for local projects. Shipping is arranged worldwide wherever freight can reach.

Clark cites a lifetime guarantee—valid for as long as the original purchaser or their family owns the piece—as a core differentiator, along with the ability to recreate any gallery design in alternative wood combinations. The founder’s design philosophy draws on the fluid forms of nature, aiming to bring the peace of the outdoors into the home.
